children: Asante withdrew its 2026 guidance of 275,000–300,000 equivalent ounces at consolidated AISC of $3,200–$3,600/oz after Bibiani underperformed. Nine-month production was 165,594 equivalent ounces at $4,308/oz; the company reported $64.0M cash and a $309.7M working capital deficiency at September 30, 2026.
The company no longer expects to meet its previously issued targets, removing a key operating benchmark.
Production and cost performance through September sets the baseline after guidance withdrawal; no prior-year consolidated comparison was provided.
The deficit and disclosed going-concern uncertainty heighten financing and liquidity risk.
Higher quarterly costs and operational issues at Bibiani contributed to the guidance withdrawal.
The plan is expected to provide remediation timelines and capital requirements, which may clarify recovery prospects.
The company is still evaluating funding alternatives; failure to meet lender plan KPIs would trigger a debt-facility event of default.

This is an operating-results update amid ongoing mine underperformance and a financing-sensitive turnaround, rather than confirmation of a stable recovery. The next catalysts are the November 30 funding deadline, Bibiani access restoration expected from Q1 2027, and the turnaround plan expected in January 2027.
from Asante Gold Corporation distributed by GlobeNewswire.
